matrix.title: Authoritative Durable State Must Be Persisted Outside Workers

temporal.rationale: History/mutable-state/outbox transaction is the authoritative durable substrate.

cadence.rationale: History and mutable state persist workflow progress and queued work.

conductor.rationale: Workflow/task DAO state drives decider progress.

airflow.rationale: DagRun/TaskInstance rows and deferred states persist lifecycle outside workers.

argo-workflows.rationale: Workflow CRD status and node maps are the durable reconciler substrate.

dagster.rationale: Run storage and event log encode execution progress.

prefect.rationale: Server-side orchestration policies validate durable state transitions.

kestra.rationale: Flow/Execution records and queue-backed Executor/Worker state persist lifecycle outside workers.

restate.rationale: Event-sourced journals and partition databases are the authoritative durable substrate.

windmill.rationale: OpenFlow step checkpoints and suspended states persist progress in PostgreSQL.

hatchet.rationale: Workflow DAG status and durable event waits persist lifecycle outside workers.

matrix.title: Single-Writer Progress Requires Fencing, Leases, Locks, or Reconciliation Tokens

temporal.rationale: RangeID shard ownership and workflow lease boundaries fence writes/reads.

cadence.rationale: RangeID is a monotonic shard ownership fence.

conductor.rationale: Workflow execution locking serializes decider progress.

airflow.rationale: Row locks and revalidation fence multi-scheduler races.

argo-workflows.rationale: Kubernetes leader election and optimistic resource-version reconciliation replace DB row locks.

dagster.rationale: Daemon-run queueing and tag concurrency limits gate launch ownership.

prefect.rationale: Server leases and DB isolation gate concurrency slots and transitions.

kestra.rationale: Flow concurrency counters and transaction retry logic fence concurrent execution/accounting races.

restate.rationale: Virtual queues serialize actor execution and Bifrost consensus fences partition leadership.

windmill.rationale: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED leases and DRR workspace scheduling fence concurrent workers.

hatchet.rationale: Slot pools, concurrency groups, and tenant fences constrain concurrent progress.

matrix.title: State Mutation and Async Work Dispatch Must Be Ordered Together

temporal.rationale: Mutable state and outbox task generation commit transactionally.

cadence.rationale: Transfer queue is a transactional outbox for side-effect tasks.

conductor.rationale: Task state must be persisted before queue removal to avoid repair duplication.

airflow.rationale: Executor dispatch and scheduler revalidation provide ordered recovery, not a classic outbox.

argo-workflows.rationale: Reconciliation from CRD/pod status couples observed state to follow-up actions.

dagster.rationale: Failure metadata and run status updates require atomic ordering.

prefect.rationale: State proposals are accepted/rejected/mutated by server policy before commit.

kestra.rationale: Typed queues decouple work dispatch while preserving execution state transitions.

restate.rationale: Journal updates and transactional outbox records are persisted together before dispatch.

windmill.rationale: Step checkpoints and queue lease assignment couple state progress with worker dispatch.

hatchet.rationale: Orchestrator status authority orders DAG state with gRPC action dispatch.

matrix.title: External Effects Are At-Least-Once Unless Application Idempotency Proves Otherwise

temporal.rationale: Activity/external side effects are not exactly-once absent application idempotency.

cadence.rationale: Async task dispatch is at-least-once and downstream handlers must be idempotent.

conductor.rationale: Queue visibility leases/redelivery imply at-least-once worker tasks.

airflow.rationale: Executor dispatch is at-least-once and requires idempotent task side effects.

argo-workflows.rationale: Pods/container execution can retry after ambiguous external effects.

dagster.rationale: Durable outputs and IOManagers are needed for safe retries/re-execution.

prefect.rationale: Transactions isolate hooks but external APIs still require compensation/idempotency.

kestra.rationale: StorageInterface references and subflow linkage isolate side-effect payloads and cancellation.

restate.rationale: Ingress idempotency keys and transactional outbox records bound external effects.

windmill.rationale: Workspace-scoped tokens and content hashes bound external/script effects.

hatchet.rationale: Durable event scope isolation and namespaced child keys provide idempotency boundaries.

matrix.title: Long Waits and Timers Need Durable Rehydration Paths

temporal.rationale: Activity retry timer regeneration preserves deadlines across replicated retries.

cadence.rationale: Cluster-local timer retry tasks must be regenerated after failover.

airflow.rationale: Deferred triggers and retry states persist wait intent.

argo-workflows.rationale: Retry/suspend state is represented in workflow/node status and reconciled.

dagster.rationale: Daemon loops and reconciliation evaluate queued/deferred work.

prefect.rationale: AwaitingRetry and Suspended states persist delay/resumption intent.

kestra.rationale: SLA timeouts and duration-bound configs persist timer/cancellation intent.

restate.rationale: TimerQueue and PromiseTable persist sleeps and awakeable callbacks.

windmill.rationale: Suspended approvals/webhooks and zombie monitoring rehydrate long waits and crashed jobs.

hatchet.rationale: Event waits, cron triggers, and lease sweeping rehydrate suspended/timed workflows.

matrix.title: Callbacks and External Events Require Dedupe and Deterministic Ordering Boundaries

temporal.rationale: Workflow task/event buffering and update validation serialize external input.

cadence.rationale: Buffered events are deduped and flushed after in-flight decisions.

conductor.rationale: Events/subworkflow callbacks target task/workflow state rather than history buffering.

airflow.rationale: Deferrable trigger events resume tasks but do not create Temporal-style signal buffering.

dagster.rationale: Asset reconciliation and sensor/event logs provide ordering at run/materialization boundaries.

prefect.rationale: Server state policy and dynamic keys isolate concurrent transitions/subflows.

kestra.rationale: Queue events and subflow cancellation paths carry ordered external lifecycle events.

restate.rationale: Service protocol suspension and awakeable resolution order external callbacks.

windmill.rationale: Webhook and approval resumptions wake suspended flow state without holding workers.

hatchet.rationale: Hierarchical event scope isolation prevents cross-workflow wakeups.

matrix.title: Retry Semantics Must Be Part of the State Machine, Not Blind Re-Enqueue

temporal.rationale: Transient workflow tasks and timer regeneration encode safe retry semantics.

cadence.rationale: Transient decision tasks prevent unbounded history growth on repeated worker failures.

conductor.rationale: Retries use delayed queue scheduling and workflow/task state.

airflow.rationale: Retry eligibility and backoff are TaskInstance state transitions.

argo-workflows.rationale: Retry/resubmit reformulates node state and must terminate wrapper nodes on shutdown.

dagster.rationale: Partial re-execution restarts failed subtrees while reusing completed outputs.

prefect.rationale: Server policy mutates Failed into AwaitingRetry with delay/jitter.

kestra.rationale: Deadlock retry and parse-time duration bounds encode retry/time behavior in the state machine.

restate.rationale: Budget deadlock recovery and durable timers are explicit runtime states.

windmill.rationale: Zombie detection and queue leases drive retry/recovery instead of blind requeue.

hatchet.rationale: Ticker lease sweeping and SDK heartbeats drive retry/recovery state.

matrix.title: Reset, Resume, and Re-Execution Must Preserve Prior Evidence

temporal.rationale: Continue/retry/parent-close mechanisms preserve history but current EKUs do not encode reset branching as directly as Cadence.

conductor.rationale: Subworkflow lifecycle synchronization resumes parent tasks without history branching.

airflow.rationale: Clearing/retry and XCom/object storage can preserve outputs but not event-history branch semantics.

argo-workflows.rationale: Retry/resubmit state reformulation preserves deterministic graph state.

dagster.rationale: Partial re-execution resumes from failed subtrees and reloads completed upstream outputs.

prefect.rationale: Suspension/resumption and result records preserve continuation boundaries.

kestra.rationale: Subflow linkage preserves parent/child evidence across cancellation and resume.

restate.rationale: Event-sourced journals preserve replay evidence for virtual actors.

windmill.rationale: Step checkpoints and asset lineage preserve evidence for resumed/backfill runs.

hatchet.rationale: Namespaced child spawn keys preserve idempotent DAG re-execution evidence.

matrix.title: High Availability Is Not a Uniform Multi-Region Semantics

temporal.rationale: Multi-cluster conflict resolution and retry timer regeneration are explicit EKU facts.

cadence.rationale: Active-passive multi-cluster requires version histories and timer regeneration.

conductor.rationale: Durability depends on persistence/queue deployment rather than repo-local version-history conflict semantics.

airflow.rationale: Multi-scheduler HA uses relational locks, not multi-region history conflict resolution.

argo-workflows.rationale: Leader-elected controller HA differs from replicated workflow history.

dagster.rationale: Daemon/launcher HA is not workflow-history multi-region failover.

prefect.rationale: Concurrency leases and work-pool recovery do not equal cross-region workflow conflict resolution.

kestra.rationale: Queue-backed microservices and gRPC worker capacity tracking provide HA semantics via queue substrate.

restate.rationale: Bifrost replicated loglets and partition storage define explicit failover semantics.

windmill.rationale: PostgreSQL worker leases and workspace fairness define HA/overload behavior without event-history replication.

hatchet.rationale: In-memory slot pools and tenant fences provide HA/overload semantics distinct from replicated history.

matrix.title: Large or Durable Payloads Should Be Referenced, Not Hidden in Execution Memory

temporal.rationale: Current EKUs emphasize history/outbox transactions, not a payload-offload solution family.

cadence.rationale: Current EKUs emphasize task/outbox persistence, not payload offload.

conductor.rationale: External payload offloading separates large workflow state from execution rows.

airflow.rationale: XCom metadata can offload large payloads to object storage.

argo-workflows.rationale: SQL archive/offloading handles workflow status scale.

prefect.rationale: ResultRecords load cached outputs from storage blocks.

kestra.rationale: StorageInterface `kestra://` references keep large inter-task payloads out of queues.

restate.rationale: Partition storage and stream-buffer decoupling keep durable payload ownership explicit.

windmill.rationale: Immutable script hashes and PostgreSQL checkpoints avoid hiding durable payload identity in worker memory.

hatchet.rationale: Worker action dispatch streams payload references through control channels rather than making memory authoritative.
